text: You could lose a war to a bird.
Australia did.
But first, Australia is wider than the moon.
Almost 4,000 kilometers wide.
The moon?
And this giant won't sit still.
It drifts 7 centimeters every year.
So in 2017, Australia officially moved itself 1.8 meters on the map.
Somewhere, a map app whispered, recalculating.
Again.
So, how do you cross something that big?
You import camels.
At least 15,000 arrived, most of them from British India.
Then trucks showed up, so the camels were set free.
Today, it has the world's biggest wild camel herd.
And it has even shipped camels to Saudi Arabia.
Desert to desert.
Business class.
But sheep farmers had a bigger enemy, dingoes.
So they built a fence, 5,614 kilometers long, longer than London to New York.
Fences stop the dogs.
Emus? They just walked through. November 1932, about 20,000 emus raid the wheat farms, so
Australia sends the army. Two machine guns, 10,000 bullets. Five weeks later, the soldiers
went home. The emus stayed. In Australia, the land is so big, the animals make the rules.
The emus? Undefeated since 1932. So yes, you really could lose a war to a bird. This is
Boogal. Follow for more geography fun facts.
